To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a fast integrated mobility spectrometer for rapid measurement and characterization of sub-micron aerosol size distributions.
the FIMS can accurately measure aerosol size distribution in the sub-micrometer range.
a new fast integrated mobility spectrometer was developed to measure the size distribution of aerosol particles in a broad dynamic range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an instrument for rapid measurement of aerosol size distribution.

the development of the FIMS, which can be used as a stand-alone instrument to measure aerosol size distribution with a dynamic range of 1–600 nm, or in combination with other aerosol instruments to measure size distributions in the overlapping range.
the development of an aerosol mobility spectrometer that can be used in the field for rapid measurement of aerosol size distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FIMS has been successfully developed, characterized and validated, and can be applied to rapid measurements of sub-micron particle size distribution.
the FIMS is an excellent tool for measuring sub-micrometer size distribution, and the FIMS can be a good alternative of the DMA-CPC combination for measuring aerosol size distribution.

the FIMS is capable of measuring the size distribution of particles with a wide dynamic range from 8 to about 600 nm, with the detection efficiency essentially 100% in the size range of 8 to about 20 nm and 200 to 600  nm, and with the transfer function and mobility resolutions well represented by the simulated values based on 2-D electric fields in the size ranges smaller than 20 nm and larger than 200 nm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FIMS is a reliable instrument for rapid aerosol measurement with size range from 8 to ∼200 nm.
the FIMS is a reliable instrument for measuring aerosol size distribution in the submicron size range.

the FIMS has a wide dynamic size detection range (10–1000 nm), a short sampling time (1 s), and a high time resolution (10–100 Hz), and can be used for rapid measurements of size distribution of atmospheric aerosols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FIMS is a robust and fast instrument for measuring sub-micrometer size distributions, with an upper size limit of 600 nm, and a lower limit of 5 nm.
the FIMS can provide a wide dynamic size distribution with a high resolution, and is capable of measuring the size distributions of ultrafine and accumulation mode aerosol particles simultaneously.
the FIMS is a robust instrument for measuring aerosol size distributions with a wide dynamic range and high temporal resolution.
